chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He عليه السلام said to me: "O Abū Muḥammad, indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not give the Prophets anything except that He had also given it to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله."
He عليه السلام said: "And He gave Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله all that He gave to the Prophets."
"And with us are the scriptures about which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ‘The scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.’"
I said, "May I be sacrificed for you, are they the Tablets?" He عليه السلام said, "Yes."

key_terms.الصُّحُفُ: the scriptures or parchments associated with earlier divine revelation
key_terms.الْأَلْوَاحُ: the Tablets, referring to the written revelation associated with Mūsā عليه السلام
key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءَ: the Prophets to whom Allah granted revelation and divine gifts
key_terms.صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى: the revealed scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā mentioned in the Qur'an
key_terms.عِنْدَنَا: in our possession, indicating custodianship by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.مُحَمَّدًا: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, who was given all prophetic endowments

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the knowledge inherited by the Imams عليهم السلام from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and the earlier Prophets?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله all that He granted to the previous Prophets, affirming his comprehensive prophetic perfection. It also indicates that the Imam possesses the inherited scriptures of earlier Prophets, including the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā, as part of the transmitted divine knowledge.
